lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Lena, you could've told me before you said I would help Owen move the display panels on Saturday.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: You're right. I should've checked with you. I saw your message saying, “I should be free,” and I treated it as a yes.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: I meant that Saturday looked possible, not that I had agreed. Owen's message made it sound final.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: I didn't mean to put you in an awkward position, but I did. That was my mistake.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Thank you for saying that. I'm frustrated because I had already promised Maya I would meet her that morning.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: I'm sorry I committed your time without asking. How can I make this right?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Please tell Owen I hadn't confirmed and that I'm not available Saturday morning.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: I'll call him now, and I'll find another volunteer. I won't ask you to explain my mistake.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Good. I could help for one hour Sunday afternoon, but please check with me before you offer that.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: Absolutely. I'll send you the exact time first. Nothing is confirmed until you reply.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: That works. The main thing is that I get to confirm my own availability.
